newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Leif Hoegh operating profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Leif Hoegh operating profits rise.

text.p: Norwegian shipping company Leif Hoegh & Co. ASA said on Thursday the strength of the car market helped increase first-half 1997 operating profits before depreciation by 14 percent to 393 million crowns.
Leif Hoegh is a large shipowner with activities in shipping of oil, gas, cars, frozen/refrigerated goods and containers.
The operation profit after depreciation increased by 50 percent to 289 million crowns, the company said in a statement.
"The higher profit was due to the strength of the car market," it said. "Hoegh Lines' result weakened while the results for the other sectors varied little from the corresponding period last year."
The result after financial items was 140 million crowns, down from 240 million in the same year-ago period, and the net profit fell to 156 million crowns from 189 million.
The company said the results were not directly comparable to the 1996 figures partly due to different depreciation rates, with ships now being depreciated over 25 years rather than 20.
Net financial items amounted to a loss of 226 million crowns compared to gains of 31 million crowns in the first half of last year.
The foreign exchange loss represented 191 million crowns, of which 126 million was unrealised.

"The foreign exchange loss is a result of the strengthening of the U.S. dollar from 6.45 crowns at the start of the year to 7.29 crowns by mid-year," Leif Hoegh said, adding that all its mortgage debt was in U.S. dollars.

The company said the prognosis from the first-quarter report for a higher operating profit this year compared to 1996 both before and after depreciation was being maintained, not least because of the strong car market.
